newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower with Treasuries on Wed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower with Treasuries on Wed.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities dipped with Treasuries on Wednesday.
Analysts cited several reasons for the decline, including futures-market technicals, another fall in stocks, foreign account selling and the lack of a Federal Reserve coupon pass.
While mortgage yield spreads over Treasuries largely held steady, movement within the market was more interesting.
Because a continuing decline in interest rates could unleash a wave of mortgage refinancings, some investors began moving down in coupon this week, traders and analysts said.
One trader said the trend would continue "at least until Friday, when we see what happens with the (payrolls) number."
One good barometer of refinancing pressure is the MBA's weekly survey, said Michael Hoeh, a senior portfolio manager at Drefus Corp.
"The index has gone from (about) 300 to 450 in five weeks," Hoeh said. "That gives you some perception of how much is potentially in the pipeline."
Further decline in interest rates would likely lead to a jump in refinancings early next year, particularly if the 10-year Treasury note's yield breaks 6.0 percent, he said.
"The only coupons that are going to be safe from refi activity are the much lower coupons, like 7.0s or 6.5s, or the very seasoned products," Hoeh said.

On Wednesday afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.0 percent coupons were off 10/32 at 99-05/32 to yield 105 basis points over the 10-year note. Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5s were off 8/32 at 100-29/32, and Freddie Mac 7.0s were down 9/32 at 99-07/32.
